item.title: DDL Doc Generator
item.description:
DDL Doc Generator

Paste MySQL CREATE TABLE statements to parse them into readable table-structure docs, exportable as Markdown. Paste several tables at once.

Everything is parsed locally in your browser — your DDL is never uploaded or sent to any server.

Table DDL

Supports backtick identifiers, and types with commas inside parentheses such as decimal(10,2) and enum('a','b').

Structure Docs

No results yet. Paste your DDL and click “Parse & Generate Docs”, or click “Load Sample” to try it out.

Kairos Lab /tools/

Local tool · No external requests

What is the DDL Doc Generator?

When writing docs, handing over a database, or doing code review, you often need a readable description of your tables. This tool parses MySQL CREATE TABLE statements into tables showing columns, types, nullability, defaults, comments, primary keys, and indexes at a glance — and exports them as Markdown. Everything is parsed locally in your browser; your DDL is never uploaded.

How to use it?

  1. Paste CREATE TABLE statements into the box on the left — several tables at once if you like. Or click “Load Sample” to see how it works.
  2. Click “Parse & Generate Docs” and the tables appear on the right.
  3. Click “Export Markdown” to save a .md file, or “Copy Markdown” to paste it straight into your docs.

item.title: VARK Learning Style Quiz
item.description:
16 questions · about 3 minutes · free · no sign-up

🧠

What is the fastest way for you to learn something? Looking at pictures, listening, reading and writing, or doing it yourself? The VARK model splits learning preferences into four styles: Visual, Aural, Read / Write, and Kinesthetic. Answer 16 everyday scenarios and find the way that works best for you.

You can pick more than one answer per question · No right or wrong · Your answers stay in your browser

Question 1 / 16

You can select more than one: pick every option that fits you

🔗 This is a quiz result shared by a friend
🎨

What is VARK?

VARK is a learning styles model by Neil Fleming from New Zealand. It groups the ways people prefer to take in information into four styles: Visual (diagrams, charts), Aural (listening, discussion), Read / Write (reading text, writing notes), and Kinesthetic (doing, practicing). No style is better than another — most people are a mix of several.

How to use your result?

  • Learn new things the way that fits you: Visual learners draw more, Aural learners talk it out, Read/Write learners take notes, Kinesthetic learners practice right away.
  • Combining styles works even better: look at a diagram first, explain it to someone, then do it yourself.
  • To go deeper into “you only learn it once you can explain it”, try the Feynman Technique: teach what you learned to someone else — if you can’t explain it, you haven’t learned it.

Note

This is a self-assessment tool with original scenario questions. The result is for reference only and is not a professional assessment.

What is the Pomodoro Technique?

The Pomodoro Technique is simple: focus for 25 minutes, then take a 5-minute break — that is one Pomodoro. After every 4 Pomodoros, take a longer 15-minute break. Short, fixed rhythms make it easier to concentrate and harder to burn out.

How to use it?

  1. Press Start and do just one thing for 25 minutes. Put your phone aside.
  2. When time is up, a popup appears and a sound plays — even if you switched to another tab, the browser notification pops up. Stand up, walk around, drink some water, and rest for 5 minutes.
  3. After 4 Pomodoros, take yourself a 15-minute long break.
  4. Your daily Pomodoro count and focus minutes are saved automatically — closing the page won’t lose them.
